card: Falls back to block policy fee estimation in the default combined estimator whenever the mempool policy estimator is unable to produce an estimate. It also introduces a 144-block warmup period after a fresh startup, failed mempool load, or block height gap, during which unfilled percentiles trigger a fallback rather than serving the relay fee floor. This prevents nodes with empty, wiped, or drained mempools from severely underestimating transaction fees or returning estimation errors when block policy estimates are readily available. No dependencies.
evidence: PR description: 'currently returns the minimum relay fee when the last saved mempool was healthy. This can be a significant underestimation, since the now-missing mempool may have held much higher-feerate transactions.'

Commit 3db35b0b4b: 'On a fresh start, or after a failed mempool load (persistence off, or a missing/corrupt mempool.dat), the estimator has no recent backlog to build on. An empty or sparse mempool makes the block-template estimate fall back to the relay floor, which can badly underbid the real fee environment.'
problem: When the combined fee estimator is queried but the mempool estimator cannot produce an estimate (such as during startup, low coverage, or while the mempool loads), it returns an error rather than falling back to the block policy estimate. Additionally, after a cold start or failed mempool reload, an empty or sparse mempool causes the mempool estimator to return the minimum relay fee floor, which can significantly underbid prevailing market fee rates.
scope_notes: About 60% of the diff consists of unit and functional tests.
summary: Falls back to the block policy fee rate estimate in the combined fee estimator when the mempool policy estimator cannot produce an estimate. Introduces a 144-block warmup period for the mempool estimator following a fresh start, failed mempool load, or block height gap. Caches un-floored block template percentiles so the estimator can distinguish an unfilled percentile from a valid floored rate during warmup.
